title: 400-1000nm Hyperspectral Leaf Reflectance Modeling for Early Discrimination of Fe vs N Chlorosis
author: Dr. vmffkxhs2362
abstract: Iron ($Fe$) and Nitrogen ($N$) deficiencies both manifest as interveinal chlorosis, rendering visual diagnosis ambiguous. We acquired 400–1000nm hyperspectral reflectance curves from mesophyll tissue under controlled nutrient depletion. A Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier trained on the Photochemical Reflectance Index ($PRI_{570/531}$) and Carotenoid Reflectance Index ($CRI_1$) differentiated Fe from N stress 7 days prior to visual symptoms with 96.8% accuracy.
key_findings: Reflectance at 705nm ($R_{705}$) shifted 12nm toward blue wavelengths during early stage Fe deficiency.
SVM classification model achieved 96.8% precision, preventing false fertilizer dosing.
Real-time edge computing cameras detected chlorosis within 12 hours of root ion depletion.
